podcast.title: Alternative Name
podcast.body: Nerdcore is also referred to by the alternative name "Geekstah Rap," highlighting its connection to geek culture within the rap idiom. "If that sounds appealing, dig around on the internet for Geekstah Wrap, that G-E-E-K-S-T-A-Rap. Geekstah Wrap, it exists."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition and Analogy
podcast.body: Nerdcore is a subgenre within the hip-hop universe, serving as the rap equivalent of what Nerd Rock is to traditional rock music. It offers a space for nerdy themes and aesthetics within the hip-hop context. "This is a corner of the hip hop universe that is to rap what Nerdrock is to regular rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hip Hop Equivalent of Nerd Rock
podcast.body: Nerdcore is described as a specific corner of the hip hop universe that functions as the rap equivalent of nerd rock, embodying a similar cultural and thematic approach within the hip hop genre. "This is a corner of the hip hop universe that is to rap what Nerdrock is to regular rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Key Artists
podcast.body: The genre of Nerdcore has roots tracing back to the Beastie Boys and includes notable artists such as MC 900 Ft. Jesus, Kool Keith, and MF Doom. "reaching back to the Beastie Boys and following through artists like MC900 for Jesus, Kulkith, MF Doom, and a whole bunch more."
